title: JaTaSn/lattice-line-covers
abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.22550: there is a family of lattice lines covering the integer plane whose set of realized directions is dense. Concretely, a family F of subsets of Z^2 is exhibited such that (i) every member is a genuine lattice line, the nonempty solution set of Px + Qy = c with P, Q coprime; (ii) the members cover Z^2; (iii) two members of different direction are disjoint, so no lattice point is covered twice in different directions; and (iv) the directions that occur are dense in the space RP^1 of line directions, that is, every angle in [0, pi) is approximated to within any epsilon by the direction of some member. The construction is recursive and works on nested regions: a chain of cosets Z^2 = R_0 > R_1 > R_2 > ... is built, and at stage k the region R_k is partitioned into sub-cosets of a new coprime direction, one of which is reserved to become R_{k+1} while lines of that direction claim all the others. Coverage is what the choice of reserved sub-coset is for: fix a surjective enumeration z_0, z_1, ... of Z^2 and reserve, at stage k, a sub-coset that does not contain z_k -- always possible, since the partition has at least four sub-cosets and only the one containing z_k must be avoided. Every point is then claimed: it is z_k for some k, and either it had already left the region at an earlier stage, in which case the coverage invariant Z^2 \ R_k = union over i < k of (R_i \ R_{i+1}) shows it was claimed there, or it is still in R_k and the reservation rule places it in a sub-coset claimed at stage k. Reserving an arbitrary sub-coset would not do: without that diagonal choice a point could survive in every R_k and never be claimed. Disjointness is a consequence of that partition rather than of any criterion for when two individual lines meet: distinct sub-cosets of a region are disjoint, each stage's lines stay inside the sub-cosets they claim, and the regions claimed at distinct stages are therefore disjoint. Earlier lines survive untouched because everything a later stage touches lies inside the reserved region. Only Theorem 1 is formalized; the paper's further remarks and discussion are not.
